_note: Stage weights are our design model (Low=1, Medium=2, High=3) based on the stage descriptions in our research doc. They are NOT NASA probabilities. 'grows' adds +1 after the middle of that stage. 'transitionBoost' sets weight 3 in the months right after a gravity change.

risks.name: Balance and motion sickness
risks.why: Your inner ear uses gravity to sense balance
risks.explain: Every time gravity changes (floating in space, landing on Mars, coming home), NASA notes dizziness and coordination problems while the brain and inner ear adapt.

risks.name: Eye and brain changes (SANS)
risks.why: Without gravity, fluids move toward your head
risks.explain: In weightlessness, blood and spinal fluid shift up. NASA links this to SANS: changes in the eyes and brain, its leading spaceflight health risk. Longer missions raise the risk.

risks.name: Bone and muscle loss
risks.why: Less weight on your body means less work for bones and muscles
risks.explain: NASA explains that when the legs don't carry the body's weight, bones and muscles weaken. That's why crews exercise every day.

risks.name: Heart and blood pressure
risks.why: Your heart is used to pumping against Earth's gravity
risks.explain: NASA studies how the heart and blood vessels adapt when gravity changes, in space, on Mars and back on Earth.

risks.name: Sleep and body clock
risks.why: Light, schedules and a different day length confuse your body clock
risks.explain: NASA lists inadequate sleep and irregular schedules as a spaceflight risk. A day on Mars lasts 24 h 39 min.

risks.name: Mood and behavior
risks.why: Months in a small space with the same few people
risks.explain: NASA says long missions can affect mood and behavior, so crews must be carefully chosen, trained and supported.

risks.name: Immune response
risks.why: A closed habitat shares the same air and microbes
risks.explain: NASA studies how spaceflight changes immune responses, and monitors microbes inside the spacecraft.

risks.name: Injury from bumps and loads
risks.why: Landing, bumps and heavy work can injure the body
risks.explain: NASA studies injuries from dynamic loads, like the forces during launch and landing, and from hard work in a suit.

risks.name: Food and nutrition
risks.why: All the food for years has to travel with you
risks.explain: NASA lists inadequate food and nutrition as a spaceflight risk: food must stay healthy and tasty for years, far from Earth.
